admission.justification: The application, CLI and landing routes must not commit or operate on a legacy line just because no converted sibling is visible; the public route matrix guards this cross-layer refusal.

applicability: Every route of the runtime that writes, checks, syncs, closes out or lands a memory line: knowledge writes, memory-quality runs, managed memory syncs, closeouts, direct landing, record landing, leaf, master and checkpoint landing, and carryover.
conditions: The route has established that its memory input lacks knowledge/layout.json; missing, unreadable and corrupt inputs retain their own errors.
exclusions: read_ar_files retains legacy cards marked legacy-format with no knowledge section, and the conversion command remains supported.
An already-current or skip-memory sync moves no memory side; an in-flight sync can continue or cancel.
A legacy target may adopt a converted source by fast-forward; mixed merges retain the crossing sync and all-converted sides retain their normal route.
A converted target cannot fast-forward from a legacy source; marker presence alone is not validator acceptance.
No absent/non-directory or definite non-repository input is fabricated into a memory line.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_knowledge_cutover.py::test_every_route_refuses_unconverted_memory_once_the_repository_holds_converted_memory; mcp/tests/test_knowledge_cutover.py::test_the_converting_candidate_is_gated_never_locked; mcp/tests/test_knowledge_cutover.py::test_a_converted_worktree_locks_too_and_an_unanswered_probe_refuses; mcp/tests/test_knowledge_cutover.py::test_only_a_definite_non_repository_reads_as_holding_no_converted_memory; review notes/reports/260928-MIK-L37-review-R1.md (R1 focus item 1 and R2: the lock at every route, 33 mutations)

statement: Every ordinary check, write, managed memory sync, closeout or landing with legacy memory input refuses with the central legacy-format conversion message whether or not converted memory exists elsewhere; named probe failures are never classified as legacy, and converted or converting candidates retain their validator and gate.
